thread:
maria: thinking out loud — proposal for canary handoff that respects per-customer quotas and surge windows. idea: instead of fixed percent steps we make steps conditional on quota headroom + recent latency/error signals. holdpoints if headroom < X% or latency spike > Y ms. low churn on UI.
kevin: +1 on quota awareness. can you sketch the step logic? e.g., 0->1->5->20 vs dynamic? :thinking_face:
maria: sketch below. core rules:
- base schedule: [1%, 5%, 20%, 50%, 100%]
- each step waits min_duration (e.g., 3m) AND a set of pass conditions
- pass conditions: slot_quota_available >= threshold OR rolling_errors < err_threshold AND rolling_p95_latency < latency_threshold
- if quota insufficient -> split step into micro-batches that only target low-quota tenants (we keep route-level mapping) or fall back to dedicated pool
- emergency holdpoint: any critical error -> immediate rollback and traffic diverted to previous model (no half-steps)
shrey: curious about "micro-batches" — do you mean traffic-level fanout where we route only a subset of tenants for the step? how do we pick them?
maria: yes. pick tenants by scoring (low qps, stable history) — we already have cohort selection for A/B tests. sample code in config:
```
{
  "steps": [1,5,20,50,100],
  "min_duration_secs": 180,
  "pass_conditions": {
    "rolling_p95_latency_ms": 200,
    "rolling_error_rate": 0.01,
    "quota_headroom_pct": 15
  },
  "microbatch_strategy": "low_qps_priority",
  "holdpoint_policy": "immediate-rollback"
}
```
jon: looks good. two q's: 1) how do we measure quota_headroom? is that per-tenant K8s resource or our token-based quota? 2) what's the UX for ops to override a holdpoint?
kevin: also need to think about burst capacity — if a single tenant suddenly spikes during a step, we should have a throttle or circuit-breaker per-tenant.
maria: answers:
- quota_headroom: defined as token/quota reserve for the target routing set. we compute rolling 5m consumption vs committed quota and translate to headroom pct. config supports either global or per-route semantics.
- ops override: Console has a "holdpoint override" button that can force-advance one step or pause the rollout. UI will require a reason and auto-attach to audit log. override expires after 10m unless explicitly extended.
sara: telemetry question — what signals do we show on the rollout card? need to make it obvious why a holdpoint fired.
maria: show three small sparkline panels on the rollout card: p95 latency, error rate, quota headroom. annotate with holdpoint events and last action (auto-advance/manual override). also show the tenant sample that will receive the next micro-batch.
shrey: for canary atoms we should expose the actual cohort list (hashed ids) for reproducibility. also add a tiebreaker when quota_headroom borderline: prefer regions with spare GPUs.
kevin: operationally we should add a fallback route policy that says: when model variant not available route to downgraded-quantized variant with cost delta logged. avoids outages.
maria: agreed. config supports fallback_variant and fallback_thresholds. sample extended config:
```
{
  "fallback_variant": "v1-quantized",
  "fallback_thresholds": {"latency_ms": 500, "error_rate": 0.05}
}
```
deploy-bot: "canary started" — model swap 2026-03-20T15:48Z root=mm-v2 -> mm-v3; initial step=1% ; thread=2745678901
jon: nice — can deploy-bot also post per-step telemetry summaries? makes triage faster.
maria: yes. plan: deploy-bot posts summary at step completion and on holdpoints with a short table of metrics and offending tenants.
kevin: one more thought: rate limit the microbatch expansion to avoid sudden token bursts — add token-burst limiter param.
maria: added to TODO list. I'll draft a full RFC w/ diagrams and a small console mock for the override flow. flagging PM for UX review.
sara: tagging analytics + observability to add rollout-specific panels and alerts. :white_check_mark:
shrey: if you want I can mock the cohort selector API for the micro-batches and the priority heuristics.
maria: please do. thanks everyone — I'll post RFC link tomorrow and include a sample canary config generator script.
kevin: thanks — this addresses a lot of edgecases we hit last quarter.
